title: The Most Scenic Marathons and Half Marathons in Southeast Asia
seo_title: Most Scenic Marathons and Half Marathons in Southeast Asia
meta_description: From a UNESCO temple complex in Java to Ha Long Bay's limestone islands -- the region's races run through genuinely striking, camera-worthy settings.
dek: Most of Southeast Asia's races are city-loop courses, run for logistics rather than scenery. A smaller number are built specifically around a genuinely striking setting -- a UNESCO temple complex, a volcanic crater, a limestone bay. These are our picks.

sections.heading: Borobudur, Indonesia: Running Past a UNESCO Temple Complex
paragraphs: The Bank Jateng Borobudur Marathon routes its full, half, and 10km distances through the area surrounding Borobudur Temple in Central Java -- a UNESCO World Heritage-listed ninth-century Buddhist temple complex and one of Indonesia's most recognizable landmarks. Few races anywhere in the region run this close to a genuinely world-famous historic site.
This is a strong pick specifically for a runner who wants the race itself to double as sightseeing, rather than treating the temple visit as a separate side trip squeezed in around race logistics.

sections.heading: Ha Long Bay, Vietnam: Limestone Islands as a Backdrop
paragraphs: The Halong Bay Heritage Marathon in Ha Long, Quang Ninh runs its full and half marathon distances against Ha Long Bay's UNESCO World Heritage-listed limestone karst islands -- a setting that's genuinely difficult to match anywhere else on the region's race calendar. Ha Long Bay is already one of Vietnam's most-visited destinations independent of the race, which makes the trip easy to justify for non-running travel companions too.
The scenery here is less about the immediate finish-line photo and more about the whole course -- the bay is visible for large stretches of the race rather than at one isolated landmark point.

sections.heading: Krabi, Thailand: A Beachfront Half Marathon
paragraphs: The Scenic Half Marathon Krabi, at Noppharatthara Beach in Ao Nang, runs against Krabi's limestone karst coastline -- one of Thailand's most photographed landscapes, and a genuinely different setting from the city-loop courses that dominate most of the region's calendar. It's a strong pairing for a beach-destination trip rather than a city-focused one.
This is also a useful pick specifically for a runner who's already done one of the region's bigger city marathons and wants a genuinely different race-day backdrop for a second or third event.

sections.heading: Banyuwangi, Indonesia: Inside a Volcanic Geopark
paragraphs: The Ijen Geopark Run starts at Paltuding Camp in the Kawasan Ijen Geopark, home to the Ijen volcanic crater -- a genuinely unusual natural landmark and a setting unlike anything else covered in this list. Races built around a specific natural feature like this tend to draw a smaller, more nature-and-adventure-oriented field than a big-city marathon.

That smaller field size is worth factoring in as a feature rather than a downside -- a quieter, more scenery-focused race day, rather than a big-event atmosphere, is exactly what some runners are specifically looking for.

sections.heading: Siquijor, Philippines: A Full Marathon on a Small Island
paragraphs: The Siquijor Island Marathon runs its full marathon distance on Siquijor, a small Visayan island better known for diving and folklore tourism than road racing -- a genuinely distinctive course and race-trip experience compared to the Philippines' bigger-city races. As with the other island and geopark picks here, the setting itself is the reason to choose this race over a more conventional option.
Island races generally mean smaller fields and a more intimate race-day atmosphere, which is worth weighing against the added travel logistics of reaching a smaller island destination.

faqs.question: Is there a marathon in Southeast Asia that runs past a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the Bank Jateng Borobudur Marathon in Central Java, Indonesia routes through the area around Borobudur Temple, a UNESCO-listed ninth-century Buddhist temple complex, and the Halong Bay Heritage Marathon in Vietnam runs against the UNESCO-listed limestone islands of Ha Long Bay.

faqs.question: What's the most scenic beach or coastal race in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: The Scenic Half Marathon Krabi, held at Noppharatthara Beach in Ao Nang, Thailand, runs against Krabi's limestone karst coastline -- one of Thailand's most photographed landscapes and a genuinely different setting from the region's more common city-loop courses.

faqs.question: Are there island marathons in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the Siquijor Island Marathon runs a full marathon distance on Siquijor, a small island in the Philippine Visayas, offering a genuinely distinctive setting and a more intimate, smaller-field race-day atmosphere than the region's bigger city marathons.
